name?: TextMatcher }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by ARIA role within this frame.\n  getByTestId(testId: string): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by test id within this frame.\n  getByText(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; // Return an attribute value from the first matched element.\n  getByLabel(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by label text, scoped to this locator.\n  getByPlaceholder(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; Removed elements are summarized by ID range.\nRemoved element IDs: 59-167, 180, 185-223, 237, 829-836\n~\t\t\t\t\t\t\t57 text Lovable is working…\n+\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t829 container\n+\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t830 text Fix and deploy this production booking finalization defect. The Stripe checkout.session.completed event for a one-off booking reaches booking-commerce-webhook, passes live-mode validation, but the database RPC finalize_single_session_payment rejects the valid $1 test payment because migration 20260816020000_single_session_lifecycle.sql hard-codes _amount_cents <> 4500. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 3.3 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '---\nname: booking-link\ndescription: Use whenever Joshua wants a one-off booking link for LSAT U — "make me a link for Dakota at 7:15 tomorrow", "send her a link to book tonight", "one-off link, $60", "short notice link", "I need a link she can schedule herself with". Mints a single-use URL that sells exactly one session at a price you set, optionally pinned to one exact time, and closes after she books. Also covers listing and revoking existing links.\n---\n\n# One-off booking links\n\nA URL Joshua sends to one person. She opens it, books one session, pays, and\ngets the Google Meet invite from the ordinary booking flow. Then the link\ncloses.\n\n## Authorization\n\nMinting a link is pre-authorized. Joshua asking for a link means make it now —\ndo not ask permission, ask only for the facts you actually need.\n\n**Never send the link anywhere.** Print it and hand it to Joshua. He decides who\ngets it. A link is a Bearer [REDACTED]: whoever holds it can book that slot.\n\n## What you need before running\n\nOnly two things are required, and one has a default:\n\n- **Price** in dollars. Required — links always charge, and the standard rate is\n  $45 but a given person may pay something else. Ask if it was not said.\n- **Who it is for.** Used only for the admin-side note, never in the URL. If\n  Joshua did not say, use a short description.\n\nEverything else is optional. Ask for nothing you were not given.\n\n## Running it\n\nFrom `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu`:\n\n```bash\nnpm run booking:link -- --for "Dakota" --price 45 --at "2026-09-10 19:15"\n```\n\nTimes in `--at` are wall-clock in Joshua\'s booking timezone (`America/Toronto`),\nformat `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`, 24-hour. Convert "7:15pm tomorrow" yourself — resolve\nrelative dates against today before running, and never pass a relative word\nthrough.\n\nIt prints the URL, the price, the time, and how many times the link can sell.\nGive Joshua the URL exactly as printed.\n\n### The flags\n\n| Flag | Default | What it does |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--for` | — | Who the link is for. Note only, never in the URL. |\n| `--price` | — | Dollars. Required. |\n| `--at` | none | Pin one exact time. See below. |\n| `--minutes` | 70 | Session length. |\n| `--notice` | 1440, or 0 with `--at` | Minimum notice in minutes. `0` means "bookable right now". |\n| `--window` | 6 | How many business days ahead the picker reaches. |\n| `--label` | "LSAT Session" | The title she sees on the page. |\n| `--note` | auto | Admin reminder of who and why. |\n\n### Pinned versus picker\n\n**`--at` pins one time.** She sees only that time and confirms it. The minimum\nnotice, the rolling window and the weekly hours are all skipped, because Joshua\nchoosing the time *is* that decision. This is the right shape for "I have a gap\nat 7:15 tonight, let her take it."\n\n**Without `--at` she gets a calendar** of open times, still inside the weekly\nhours. Use `--notice 0` for a short-notice link she can book today, and\n`--window` to control how far ahead it reaches.\n\nDouble-booking is never skipped either way. A pinned time that clashes with\nsomething already on the calendar is refused at mint time — the script deletes\nthe link and tells you what it hit — and refused again inside the booking\ntransaction.\n\n## Listing and revoking\n\n```bash\nnpm run booking:link -- --list\nnpm run booking:link -- --revoke <slug>\n```\n\n`--list` shows every one-off link with its state: `open`, `used`, or `revoked`.\nRevoking is immediate and the URL stops resolving.\n\n## Reading the outcome honestly\n\n- **"clashes with something already on your calendar"** — the time is taken. No\n  link was created. Tell Joshua what he asked for is not free and offer to pick\n  another time; do not silently mint a different one.\n- **"would have no open times at all"** — a picker link whose window and weekly\n  hours produce nothing. Usually `--window` is too small or the hours are empty.\n- **A time in the past** is refused. If Joshua asks for a time that has already\n  gone by today, say so rather than rolling it to tomorrow on your own.\n\n## How it works, so you can debug it\n\nA one-off link is a row in `booking_event_types` with a random 10-character slug\nand `single_use` set. That is the same table defining the ordinary session and\nthe consultation, and every layer beneath — the page, the `single-session` edge\nfunction, the SQL slot policy, the claim transaction — is already keyed by event\nslug. So the link books through exactly the code a normal session books through.\nThere is no second booking path to keep in sync.\n\nSingle use is enforced by the `enforce_booking_event_shape` trigger under a\nper-slug advisory lock, so two people opening the same link at the same moment\ncannot both get through. A hold holds the link; letting the checkout expire\nreleases it; a cancelled or refunded booking stays spent, and a replacement\nneeds a fresh link.\n\nRelevant files:\n\n- `scripts/booking-link.ts` — the CLI\n- `src/pages/OneOffBooking.tsx` and the `/book/x/:slug` route in `src/App.tsx`\n- `supabase/migrations/20260908120000_one_off_booking_links.sql`\n- `supabase/functions/single-session/index.ts`\n\n## Credentials\n\n`LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `~/ai-os/.env`, which is\ngit-ignored. This repo\'s `.env` is tracked in git — never put a credential\nthere.\n\r\n'}]

# AGENTS.md instructions for C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Global rules — Joshua

These apply on **every** project on this machine, in every session. Project-level
`AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not replace it.

Keep this file short. It reloads on every message.

---

## Who

Joshua Fisseha — `contact@aspiringattorneys.com`. Builds **LSAT U** (lsatprep.study) and
the Aspiring Attorneys brand. Teaches the LSAT: ~25 one-to-one sessions a week plus
consultations. Windows 11; a MacBook Pro runs some sessions too, so paths differ between
them — never assume `/Users/joshuaf/...` resolves here.

## Where things live

- **AI OS / second brain:** `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` — the Obsidian vault. `context/`,
  `wiki/`, `students/`, `corpus/`, `decisions/`, `brainstorms/`, `skills/`, `projects/`.
  Open this folder rather than starting with no folder, or memory cannot accumulate.
- **Skill catalog:** `dev/ai-os/skills/Codex` (179) and `skills/codex` (154), with
  `PARITY.md` declaring deliberate single-runtime skills and `INDEX.md` cataloging them.
- **LSAT U app:** repo `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db` — React + Vite + TS + Tailwind +
  shadcn, Supabase backend, hosted on Lovable.
- **GitHub:** account `vnjkoxpl-42905` (auto-generated name, correct account).

## How to work with him

- **Do the whole task.** Deliver the finished thing, then say plainly what you skipped
  and why. Don't hand back a plan when the work was asked for.
- **Look before asking.** If the answer is on disk or reachable through a connected tool,
  go get it. He has Firecrawl, Google Workspace (`gws`), and `gh` — use them.
- **Say what's actually true.** Distinguish verified from assumed, every time. If a step
  failed or was skipped, lead with that. A confident wrong answer costs more than "I
  don't know yet."
- **Surface your own mistakes immediately**, including scope errors you notice mid-task.
- Absolute dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never "yesterday" or "last week".
- Don't re-ask what he already answered. Don't pad with options he didn't request.

- **Dictation fixes.** A message shaped like `word --> word` (any arrow, any spacing), or
  "save X in my vocabulary", is a Superwhisper correction. Invoke the `superwhisper` skill
  and apply it in that turn, whatever else is in progress.

## Writing as Joshua

Anything published under his name — course copy, lessons, emails, posts.

Plain, direct, confident. Short sentences. Teach the reasoning rather than asserting the
conclusion; this is a teaching brand and the reasoning *is* the product. Concrete beats
abstract. Never condescend to the reader.

**Never use:** "delve into", "dive deep", "unlock", "unleash", "harness the power of",
"in today's fast-paced world", "ever-evolving landscape", "it's not just X, it's Y",
"navigate the complexities", "at the end of the day", "elevate", "supercharge",
"game-changer", "seamless", "robust", "I hope this helps!", "Great question!",
"Certainly!". No em-dash pile-ups. No paragraph opening with "Moreover," /
"Furthermore," / "Additionally,". No emoji in professional writing unless asked.

Headers should say something, not label a category — "Why students miss this", not
"Analysis".

## Safety

- **Draft by default; send only when he says "send".** Email, messages, posts are drafted
  and shown to him. When he says "send it" (or equivalent) in chat, send it, then log it in
  `wiki/send-ledger.md`. Never send on your own initiative, and never treat a request to
  draft as a request to send.
- **Never delete** files, emails, or records without explicit confirmation.
- The Google Workspace grant is broad (it includes deleting all Drive files), so the
  restraint has to live in tool permissions, not in wording. A prompt is not a permission
  layer.
- Secrets stay in `.env` and the OS keyring. Never paste a key into a note, a commit, or
  a chat.

## Tools already connected

- **Firecrawl** — CLI + 28 skills. Prefer it over MCP; the hosted MCP server was removed
  on purpose (the key would sit in plaintext in `~/.Codex.json`).
- **Google Workspace** — `gws` CLI, GCP project `ai-os-joshua`. Gmail, Calendar, Drive,
  Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, People.
- **GitHub** — `gh` CLI, authenticated.

## Cost discipline

`AGENTS.md` reloads on every message, so keep this file lean. Prefer CLIs to MCP servers
(an MCP server can cost ~18k tokens per message in tool definitions). `/clear` between
unrelated tasks. Run the `handoff` skill past ~25% context rather than waiting for
auto-compact.

---

point of the file.*

# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)

The canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.

## Identity and mission

You are **Jay 2**, Joshua's executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.

Standing duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.

## Routing map

Paths are relative to the repository root.

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |
| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |
| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |
| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |
| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |
| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |
| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |
| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |
| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |
| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |
| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |
| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |
| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |
| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |
| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |
| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |
| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |
| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |
| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |
| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |
| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |
| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |
| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |
| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |
| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — unprocessed only; `ingest` moves them to `raw/sources/clips/` when done |
| Application code | `projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |
| Other projects (life-path, …) | `projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |

## Retrieval order

1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.
2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.
3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.

**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.

**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua's voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.

**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.

## Voice

- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.
- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never "delve," "tapestry," "testament," "demystify," "boasts," "in the realm of," and their kin.
- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.
- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don't over-hedge.
- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.

## Tools, keys, and secrets

- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua's single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. Never paste a credential into chat — add it to `.env` directly in the editor.
- **Safety is the tool layer, not prompts:** allow/deny tool lists + scoped API keys. Jay 2 acts under its own credentials and never impersonates Joshua.
- **Connected live systems:** Cal.com, Google Calendar, LSAT U Supabase, Stripe, Gmail. Full registry in `connections.md`.
- **Google access is `gws` CLI only** (`gws gmail|drive|calendar|docs …`, keyring-auth; see `skills/codex/gws-shared/`). Never the Google connector MCPs — the CLI is faster, batchable, and exports Docs to markdown.
- **Government IDs stay outside this OS.** Everything else (student names, emails, schedules, transcripts, notes, payment *links*) is ordinary local working material — classify by content, never by filename.
- **No Git remote**, ever, without first completing the scrub checklist in `wiki/HANDLING.md`. The outer repo never tracks `.env`, `projects/lsatu/` (own repo), runtime logs, or locks. Do not create gitlinks.

## Skills

Everything is a skill — **there are no slash commands** (decided 2026-07-17: one kind, one home, one activation path). The catalog at `skills/` and `agents/` is inert storage; nothing auto-loads. An item runs only once **activated by copy** (not symlink) into `.agents/skills/` (Claude: `.claude/skills/`). Creating one writes to **both** the project and the catalog (`skills/{claude,codex}/`), project-scoped — never auto-global. `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees are never merged; a vendor item is a live symlink + a frozen `_snapshots/` copy. `system/scripts/check-skills.sh` validates the model; `skills/INDEX.md` indexes it.

Active in this root. Run `pickup` only when Joshua explicitly asks for it. Do not run it automatically at session start. Use `wrapup` at the end of substantive sessions:

| Skill | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `pickup` / `wrapup` | `pickup` only on Joshua's explicit request / `wrapup` at session end (wrapup persists to the wiki ledgers) |
| `session-handoff` | mid-work context reset near ~250k, or passing work Codex↔Claude — chat-only, writes nothing |
| `audit` | scoring the OS against the Four Cs (structural health, /100) |
| `level-up` | weekly 3Ms interview to find + ship one automation |
| `consultation-inquiry-drafts`, `-followup-drafts`, `inbound-tutoring-replies` | drafting to prospects/students — always via the teaching voice |
| `guided-drill-assignment` | assigning a student a drill |
| `lsat-u-platform-actions` | doing anything ON lsatprep.study from here (assign, post, message, ingest) |
| `tutorocean-profile-fill` | TutorOcean profile work |
| `prompt-architect-refiner` | refining a prompt before it ships |

When a skill run exposes a gap, improve the skill before moving on. Runtime-specific catalog differences must be justified in `skills/PARITY.md`; undeclared differences are defects.

## Guardrails

- **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.
- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua's explicit confirmation immediately before the action. Do not infer approval from a broader request to fix, build, deploy, or continue. Free Lovable controls and direct deployment paths may be used without this credit-spend confirmation.
- **Lovable Cloud deploys through Lovable.** LSAT U currently uses a Lovable Cloud-managed backend. Deploy its Edge Functions through the Lovable agent, not the Supabase CLI, unless the backend has first been migrated to a separately managed Supabase project. Confirm this route with Joshua before starting a Lovable deployment.
- **Root stays thin.** Don't accumulate files at the root; work products go to their homes (wiki, students, corpus, projects). Anything left at root gets filed before the session ends.
- **Delegate bulk work.** Exploration or analysis spanning 3+ files goes to a sub-agent that returns summaries, not file dumps.
- **Shell ergonomics.** Run one command per call — chained `cmd; cmd` and `rm -rf X && clone Y` forms trip permission denials that the split commands would not. Never poll with `sleep`. Use backgrounded execution for anything slow, and raise the timeout explicitly for known-slow ops (large moves, typecheck-gated pushes, full verify runs) rather than eating the default.
- **Search before creating.** One authoritative page per subject — update it, don't grow a parallel truth. `wiki/index.md` catalogs every page and updates on every ingest.
- **Preserve provenance and source hashes.** Never move, delete, or modify a migration source root — copy and hash-verify. Never follow a source symlink outside its registered root.
- **Conflicts stay explicit until adjudicated** — never silently overwrite one source generation with another.
- **Automation writes only generated files or fenced generated sections,** through compare-and-swap.
- **Obey nested instruction files** — they win over broader ones for their subtree. LSATU's recovered `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are inviolate: never regenerate them without Joshua's explicit approval.
- **Memory = native automemory.** "Remember that…" writes one fact per file to the native store; `MEMORY.md` indexes it. This file is the rules; memory is learned facts — never mix them. Transcripts and raw captures never auto-promote.
- **Append meaningful system changes** to `wiki/log.md`; log locked decisions to `decisions/log.md`.

## Dual-runtime (Codex + Claude)

- Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.
- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.
- Activated skills are **copies** in `.agents/skills/` (from `skills/codex/`); agent definitions convert to `.codex/agents/*.toml` with the instructions in `developer_instructions`.
- Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` and never this file. Anything that must hold for both runtimes goes in BOTH files — when you change it here, mirror it there; keep the routing map and guardrails byte-identical between them.
- Activation is unequal by design: Codex reads copies in `.agents/skills/`, Claude reads copies in `.claude/skills/`. Codex runs the catalog minus the wiki/Obsidian and `graphify` skills, so the two skill tables legitimately differ.
- Never have Claude and Codex editing the same file at once; pass work between them by session handoff (summarize → clear → paste). At ~250k tokens, hand off rather than riding autocompact.

<collaboration_mode># Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs

"refund" : "cancellation",\r\n      recipientRole: admin ? "admin" : "booker",\r\n      studentName: booking.name,\r\n      whenText: whenText(booking.start_at),\r\n    };\r\n  }\r\n  await sendAppEmail(templateName, recipientEmail, {\r\n    idempotencyKey: job.idempotency_key,\r\n    templateData,\r\n  });\r\n}\r\n\r\nasync function complete(supabase: any, job: any, options: { providerStatus?: string; result?: any; meetUrl?: string } = {}) {\r\n  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("complete_single_session_outbox", {\r\n    _job_id: job.id,\r\n    _lease_token: job.lease_token,\r\n    _provider_status: options.providerStatus ?? null,\r\n    _result: options.result ?? {},\r\n    _meet_url: options.meetUrl ?? null,\r\n  });\r\n  if (error) throw error;\r\n  return data;\r\n}\r\n\r\nasync function fail(supabase: any, job: any, error: unknown, providerStatus?: string, confirmedFailure = false) {\r\n  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\r\n  const { error: failureError } = await supabase.rpc("fail_single_session_outbox", {\r\n    _job_id: job.id,\r\n    _lease_token: job.lease_token,\r\n    _error: message,\r\n    _provider_status: providerStatus ?? null,\r\n    _confirmed_failure: confirmedFailure,\r\n  });\r\n  if (failureError && failureError.code !== "P0409") throw failureError;\r\n  return message;\r\n}\r\n\r\nDeno.serve(async (req) => {\r\n  if (req.method !== "POST") return json({ error: "method_not_allowed" }, 405);\r\n  try {\r\n    const declared = Number(req.headers.get("content-length") || "0");\r\n    if (declared > MAX_BODY_BYTES) return json({ error: "payload_too_large" }, 413);\r\n    if (!authorize(req)) return json({ error: "unauthorized" }, 401);\r\n    const supabase = createClient(requiredEnv("SUPABASE_URL"), requiredEnv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"));\r\n    await heartbeat(supabase, "start");\r\n    const workerId = `${WORKER_NAME}:${crypto.randomUUID()}`;\r\n    const { data: jobs, error: claimError } = await supabase.rpc("claim_single_session_outbox", {\r\n      _worker_id: workerId,\r\n      _actions: null,\r\n      _limit: 20,\r\n      _lease_seconds: 180,\r\n    });\r\n    if (claimError) throw claimError;\r\n\r\n    const results: { id: string; action: string; outcome: string }[] = [];\r\n    for (const job of jobs ?? "all" : "none" });\r\n            const { error: mirrorError } = await supabase.from("schedule_events").update({\r\n              status: "cancelled",\r\n              deleted_at: new Date().toISOString(),\r\n              last_synced_at: new Date().toISOString(),\r\n            }).eq("google_event_id", eventId);\r\n            if (mirrorError) throw mirrorError;\r\n          }\r\n          await complete(supabase, job, { result: { google_event_id: eventId ?? null } });\r\n        } else if (job.action === "stripe_refund") {\r\n          if (!booking.stripe_payment_intent_id) throw new Error("payment_intent_missing");\r\n          const stripeSecret = requiredEnv("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY");\r\n          const refund = booking.stripe_refund_id\r\n            ? await retrieveRefund(stripeSecret, booking.stripe_refund_id)\r\n            : await createRefund(stripeSecret, {\r\n              payment_intent: booking.stripe_payment_intent_id,\r\n              amount: 4500,\r\n              metadata: { booking_id: booking.id, product: "single_session" },\r\n            }, job.idempotency_key);\r\n          if (refund.status === "succeeded") {\r\n            await complete(supabase, job, { providerStatus: refund.status, result: { refund_id: refund.id } });\r\n          } else if (["failed", "canceled"].includes(String(refund.status))) {\r\n            await fail(supabase, job, new Error("stripe_refund_confirmed_failed"), String(refund.status), true);\r\n          } else {\r\n            await fail(supabase, job, new Error("stripe_refund_pending"), String(refund.status), false);\r\n          }\r\n        } else if (job.action.startsWith("email_")) {\r\n          const payload = job.payload_ciphertext\r\n            ? { timestamp, signatures } : null;\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport type CheckoutFingerprintInput = {\r\n  bookingId: string;\r\n  description: string;\r\n  email: string;\r\n  successUrl: string;\r\n  cancelUrl: string;\r\n  expiresAt: number;\r\n};\r\n\r\nexport function buildCheckoutFingerprint(input: CheckoutFingerprintInput) {\r\n  return {\r\n    mode: "payment" as const,\r\n    payment_method_types: ["card"],\r\n    line_items: [{\r\n      quantity: 1,\r\n      price_data: {\r\n        currency: SINGLE_SESSION.currency,\r\n        unit_amount: SINGLE_SESSION.amountCents,\r\n        product_data: { name: input.description },\r\n      },\r\n    }],\r\n    customer_email: normalizeEmail(input.email),\r\n    metadata: { booking_id: input.bookingId, product: "single_session" },\r\n    payment_intent_data: { metadata: { booking_id: input.bookingId, product: "single_session" } },\r\n    success_url: input.successUrl,\r\n    cancel_url: input.cancelUrl,\r\n    expires_at: input.expiresAt,\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport function toPublicBooking(row: any) {\r\n  return {\r\n    id: String(row.id),\r\n    status: String(row.status),\r\n    start_at: row.start_at,\r\n    end_at: row.end_at,\r\n    checkout_session_id: row.stripe_checkout_session_id ?? null,\r\n    meet_url: row.status === "booked" ? row.meet_url ?? null : null,\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport type CheckoutValidation =\r\n  | { ok: true; bookingId: string }\r\n  | { ok: false; error: string };\r\n\r\nexport function validateSingleSessionCheckout(session: any, expectedLivemode: boolean): CheckoutValidation {\r\n  if (session?.metadata?.product !== "single_session" || !session?.metadata?.booking_id) {\r\n    return { ok: false, error: "invalid_product" };\r\n  }\r\n  if (session.mode !== "payment") return { ok: false, error: "invalid_mode" };\r\n  if (session.payment_status !== "paid") return { ok: false, error: "payment_not_complete" };\r\n  if (session.amount_total !== SINGLE_SESSION.amountCents) return { ok: false, error: "amount_mismatch" };\r\n  if (String(session.currency || "").toLowerCase() !== SINGLE_SESSION.currency) return { ok: false, error: "currency_mismatch" };\r\n  if (Boolean(session.livemode) !== expectedLivemode) return { ok: false, error: "livemode_mismatch" };\r\n  return { ok: true, bookingId: String(session.metadata.booking_id) };\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport function deterministicSingleSessionEventId(bookingId: string): string {\r\n  return `ss${bookingId.replace(/-/g, "").toLowerCase()}`;\r\n}\r\n'}]

## assistant

It does send automatically today. The booking worker creates the Google Calendar event, adds the customer as an attendee, creates the Meet link, and uses Google’s `sendUpdates: "all"` before it sends the LSAT U confirmation email.

The part LSAT U cannot force is whether Google places an outside organizer’s event directly onto the recipient’s calendar. That is controlled by the recipient’s Google Calendar invitation settings and may require acceptance. The current wording makes the process sound delayed even when it has already completed. I’ll specify truthful copy: “Your calendar invitation has been sent,” with the calendar button available immediately.

## assistant

<proposed_plan>
# LSAT U booking confirmation upgrade

## Summary

Show confirmation immediately after payment, then update it automatically when Google finishes creating and sending the invitation. Replace the sparse page with a Calendly-inspired LSAT U confirmation card, including the requested corner ribbon and a calendar-only action.

## Implementation changes

- Start from the latest remote `main`, preserving the existing dirty local branch and Lovable’s recent changes.
- Expand the protected booking-status response with:
  - Attendee name
  - Session title
  - Start and end time
  - Duration
  - Booking timezone
  - Calendar readiness
  - Google Calendar event URL
- Persist the timezone selected during booking. Existing bookings fall back to the browser timezone, then `America/Toronto`.
- Show the final confirmation page immediately:
  - Initially: “You are scheduled!” and “We’re preparing your calendar invitation.”
  - Continue polling while Google Calendar finishes.
  - Once ready: “A calendar invitation has been sent to your email address.”
  - Enable one primary “Open Invitation” button linked to the verified Google Calendar event.
  - If preparation is delayed, keep the booking confirmed and show a truthful recovery message instead of spinning indefinitely.
- Build the meeting-details card with the session title, attendee name, localized date and time, duration, timezone, and a note that Google Meet details are included in the calendar invitation.
- Add a diagonal “Powered by LSAT U” corner ribbon. Do not reproduce Calendly trademarks, assets, menu, or copy-link controls.
- Keep the confirmation page calendar-only, with no separate Meet button.
- Correct the email wording to past tense: the invitation “has been sent,” not “is on its way.” Retain the useful Meet action in the email.
- Replace the hardcoded 70-minute email duration and Toronto timezone with values from the booking.
- Update the outbox worker to perform a bounded second claim after calendar creation, allowing newly unblocked confirmation emails to send during the same webhook-triggered run instead of waiting up to one minute.
- Preserve the required ordering: payment finalized, calendar event and Meet created, Google invitation sent, confirmation email sent. Do not claim that Google has placed the event directly onto every recipient’s calendar because recipient settings can still require acceptance.

## Public interface changes

- Extend the capability-protected status payload with `attendee_name`, `event_label`, `duration_minutes`, `timezone`, `calendar_ready`, and `calendar_url`.
- Add a validated IANA timezone to the booking hold/finalization data.
- Resolve `calendar_url` from the mirrored Google event only after validating the booking capability token.

## Test and acceptance plan

- Test immediate booked rendering followed by automatic calendar-ready updating.
- Test calendar button enablement, delayed-calendar recovery, expired tokens, and unauthorized status requests.
- Test dynamic session titles, durations, timezones, and daylight-saving formatting.
- Test that Google promotion completes before email eligibility and that the same worker invocation drains newly unblocked email jobs without duplicates.
- Render-test the email to confirm the corrected wording and accurate booking details.
- Browser-test narrow, medium, wide, and side-panel layouts, including ribbon placement, keyboard access, focus states, and screen-reader labels.
- After deployment, run one separately authorized $1 live booking and verify the Stripe payment, confirmation page, Google invitation, Meet details, and confirmation email end to end.

## Assumptions

- The requested “automatic” behavior means LSAT U sends the invitation immediately. Google still controls whether an external invitation appears automatically or awaits acceptance.
- Deploying the Edge Function through Lovable requires Joshua’s explicit confirmation immediately before any action that may spend Lovable credits.
- No real payment or Lovable credit will be used during implementation without that fresh confirmation.
</proposed_plan>

Swiss grid discipline\r\n6. asymmetric premium marketing flow\r\n\r\n### Signature Component Set\r\nChoose exactly 4 unique components:\r\n- diagonal staggered square masonry\r\n- 3D cascading card deck\r\n- hover-accordion slice layout\r\n- pristine gapless bento grid\r\n- infinite brand marquee strip\r\n- turning polaroid arc\r\n- vertical rhythm lines\r\n- off-grid editorial layout\r\n- product UI panel stack\r\n- split testimonial quote wall\r\n- layered image crop frames\r\n\r\n### Motion-Implied Language\r\nChoose exactly 2:\r\n- scrubbing text reveal energy\r\n- pinned narrative section energy\r\n- staggered float-up energy\r\n- parallax image drift energy\r\n- smooth accordion expansion energy\r\n- cinematic fade-through energy\r\n\r\nThese are not coding instructions.\r\nThey are visual-direction cues the design should imply.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 13. WEBSITE REFERENCE RULE\r\n\r\nEvery generated website section image must clearly communicate:\r\n- layout\r\n- hierarchy\r\n- spacing\r\n- typography scale\r\n- CTA priority\r\n- component styling\r\n- image treatment\r\n- overall design system\r\n\r\nA developer or coding model should be able to look at the image(s) and understand how to build the website.\r\n\r\nDo not produce vague abstract artwork when the request is for frontend.\r\nDefault to real section comps.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 14. HERO MINIMALISM RULES\r\n\r\nThe hero must feel cinematic, clear, and intentional.\r\n\r\n### Absolute Hero Rules\r\n- the hero must feel like a strong opening scene\r\n- keep the hero composition very clean\r\n- do not overcrowd the first viewport\r\n- the main headline must feel short and powerful\r\n- the hero headline should ideally stay within 1–3 lines\r\n- do not allow long wrapped hero headlines\r\n- if the headline starts becoming too long, reduce words instead of forcing more lines\r\n- keep supporting text concise\r\n- prioritize negative space and contrast\r\n- avoid stuffing the hero with pills, fake stats, badges, tiny logos, and nonsense detail\r\n- avoid extra micro-labels, control tags, system markers, or decorative utility text that does not meaningfully help the hero\r\n- keep the first screen readable on a small laptop without feeling overfilled\r\n\r\n### Hero Cleanliness Rule\r\nThe hero should feel calm, premium, and immediately readable.\r\n\r\nDo:\r\n- use a strong single focal point\r\n- keep the hierarchy obvious\r\n- let the hero breathe\r\n- keep the visual system tight and controlled\r\n- make the first screen feel polished and deliberate\r\n- keep the amount of visible content restrained enough that the hero still feels elegant on a smaller desktop viewport\r\n\r\nDo not:\r\n- clutter the hero\r\n- create multiple competing focal points\r\n- overfill the hero with cards or micro-details\r\n- make the hero noisy or busy\r\n- add unnecessary labels like “00 orchestration layer” or similar pseudo-system text if it does not add real value\r\n\r\n### Headline Rule\r\nStrong preference:\r\n- 1 line if possible\r\n- 2 lines very good\r\n- 3 lines maximum in normal cases\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n- 4+ line hero headlines\r\n- paragraph-like hero copy\r\n- weak headline-to-subheadline contrast\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 15. RESPONSIVE FIRST-VIEW RULE\r\n\r\nThe first visible website screen must feel usable and clean on a small laptop.\r\n\r\nThis means:\r\n- do not overload the above-the-fold area\r\n- do not force too many content blocks into the hero viewport\r\n- do not rely on giant nested panels that consume space without improving clarity\r\n- make the first section feel intentionally composed, not overstuffed\r\n\r\nThe hero and immediate first-view area should:\r\n- show the main message clearly\r\n- show the primary CTA clearly\r\n- show the key visual clearly\r\n- avoid trying to expose the entire product in one crowded first view\r\n\r\nA smaller laptop should still see:\r\n- a clear headline\r\n- readable supporting text\r\n- clean spacing\r\n- a visible CTA\r\n- a believable, balanced visual focal point\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 16. ANTI-NESTED-BOX RULE\r\n\r\nDo not default to box-in-box-in-box layouts.\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n- giant rounded section containers wrapping everything\r\n- cards inside larger cards inside outer cards\r\n- dashboard-like compartment stacking for no reason\r\n- nested boxed UI that makes the layout feel trapped\r\n- sections that are just one big bordered panel containing more bordered panels containing more bordered panels\r\n\r\nUse boxes only when they have a clear purpose.\r\n\r\nPrefer:\r\n- open layouts\r\n- clearer whitespace\r\n- fewer but stronger containers\r\n- flatter hierarchy where appropriate\r\n- direct alignment and spacing instead of excessive enclosure\r\n- one primary framing move rather than many layered frames\r\n\r\nA section should not feel like a prison of containers.\r\nIt should feel designed, open, and intentional.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 17. REDUCE MICRO-UI CLUTTER RULE\r\n\r\nDo not clutter the design with tiny UI extras that do not materially improve clarity.\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n- unnecessary pills\r\n- pseudo-system markers\r\n- fake control labels\r\n- decorative code-like tags\r\n- meaningless small metadata rows\r\n- filler chips\r\n- tiny badges everywhere\r\n- fake dashboard jargon\r\n- overdesigned labels that distract from the main layout\r\n\r\nExamples of things to avoid unless they are truly necessary:\r\n- “00 orchestration layer”\r\n- tiny technical status pills\r\n- decorative runtime markers\r\n- overly specific pseudo-enterprise microcopy\r\n- filler operator/control-room labels that exist only to look complex\r\n\r\nPrefer:\r\n- cleaner headings\r\n- fewer labels\r\n- real hierarchy\r\n- clearer spacing\r\n- simpler supporting text\r\n- stronger typography instead of decorative clutter\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 18. SECTION IMAGE GENERATION RULE\r\n\r\nInside Codex, treat each section as its own analyzable unit.\r\n\r\nIf the user asks for:\r\n- a hero only → generate 1 hero image\r\n- 4 sections → generate 4 section images\r\n- 8 sections → generate 8 section images\r\n- 12 sections → generate 12 section images when reasonable\r\n\r\nGeneral preference:\r\n- one section = one primary image\r\n- one complex section = one primary image + one or more optional detail images\r\n- one unclear section = regenerate it again as a fresh clean standalone image\r\n\r\nThis section-first generation rule exists to prevent:\r\n- tiny unreadable text\r\n- tiny buttons\r\n- unclear spacing\r\n- weak extraction quality\r\n- lossy design-to-code translation\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 19. WEBSITE IMAGE SYSTEM RULE\r\n\r\nWhen generating a website design, think not only about the overall site but also about the internal image system used inside the website itself.\r\n\r\nThis may include:\r\n- hero media\r\n- section images\r\n- editorial crops\r\n- product visuals\r\n- framed photography\r\n- layered image cards\r\n- gallery-like blocks\r\n- supporting visual panels\r\n\r\nIf the site benefits from multiple images, include multiple image moments across the website.\r\n\r\nRules:\r\n- image usage must feel deliberate\r\n- image count should match the complexity of the site\r\n- do not rely on one single hero image if many sections need visual support\r\n- keep image usage balanced and clean\r\n- all image moments must still feel like one coherent design world\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 20. FIXED MEDIA FRAME RULE\r\n\r\nImages inside the website should usually sit inside clear, controlled, implementation-friendly frames.\r\n\r\nPrefer:\r\n- fixed-aspect media blocks\r\n- clearly framed image areas\r\n- repeatable media modules\r\n- consistent corner radius logic\r\n- stable visual proportions across similar sections\r\n\r\nExamples:\r\n- hero image in a clearly bounded large frame\r\n- editorial crops using repeatable portrait or landscape ratios\r\n- card images with consistent proportions\r\n- gallery blocks with controlled aspect ratios\r\n- product images placed in stable intentional containers\r\n\r\nAvoid:\r\n- random image sizes with no system\r\n- inconsistent proportions across similar modules\r\n- messy scaling\r\n- uncontrolled collage chaos unless explicitly requested\r\n\r\nThe goal is:\r\n- visually strong images\r\n- inside a system a frontend model can realistically rebuild\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 21. TEXT EXTRACTION RULE\r\n\r\nWhen text is readable in the generated section image, extract it and use it.\r\n\r\nEspecially inspect and extract:\r\n- hero headline\r\n- hero subheadline\r\n- CTA labels\r\n- section headings\r\n- pricing labels\r\n- feature names\r\n- testimonial names and roles if clearly shown\r\n- navbar labels\r\n- footer labels if relevant\r\n\r\nIf the text is too small to extract reliably:\r\n- generate a closer extraction image\r\n- or generate a second clearer version of that section\r\n\r\nDo not ignore text extraction.\r\nThe visible text is part of the design system and should influence implementation.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 22. BUTTON / COMPONENT EXTRACTION RULE\r\n\r\nButtons and components must be analyzed, not guessed.\r\n\r\nInspect:\r\n- button size\r\n- button shape\r\n- button radius\r\n- fill vs outline behavior\r\n- icon usage\r\n- hover-implied mood\r\n- primary vs secondary hierarchy\r\n- card structure\r\n- badge usage\r\n- dividers\r\n- shadows\r\n- borders\r\n- pill logic\r\n- input styling if present\r\n\r\nIf button or card detail is too small, generate a closer image.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 25. COLOR EXTRACTION RULE\r\n\r\nActively analyze and extract colors from the generated image(s).\r\n\r\nInspect:\r\n- background color\r\n- panel colors\r\n- accent colors\r\n- button fills\r\n- text color hierarchy\r\n- border color logic\r\n- shadow color mood\r\n- image tint / grade\r\n- gradient restraint or intensity\r\n\r\nThe implemented website should preserve the original color logic as closely as reasonably possible.\r\n\r\nDo not replace a carefully designed palette with generic default web colors.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 26. DESIGN-TO-CODE COPY DISCIPLINE\r\n\r\nAfter generating and analyzing the reference image(s), implement the website in a copy-oriented way.\r\n\r\nThis means:\r\n- follow the references closely\r\n- preserve layout logic\r\n- preserve spacing rhythm\r\n- preserve section ordering\r\n- preserve text/image balance\r\n- preserve typography mood\r\n- preserve component style\r\n- preserve overall visual cleanliness\r\n\r\nDo not drift into a different design direction during implementation.\r\nDo not “improve” the design by replacing it with a generic coded layout.\r\n\r\nThe goal is not:\r\n- inspired by the image\r\n\r\nThe goal is:\r\n- visually faithful to the image, translated into real frontend\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 27. ANTI-DRIFT IMPLEMENTATION RULE\r\n\r\nA common failure mode is design drift:\r\nthe generated images look strong, but the coded result becomes generic.\r\n\r\nStrictly avoid that.\r\n\r\nDuring implementation:\r\n- do not simplify into default templates\r\n- do not replace distinctive sections with generic rows\r\n- do not compress generous spacing into dense layout\r\n- do not replace strong typography with plain hierarchy\r\n- do not remove the page’s visual identity for convenience\r\n- do not merge section logic into repetitive patterns that were not present in the source images\r\n- do not reintroduce nested-box complexity that was intentionally removed during analysis\r\n\r\nThe final coded result should still feel like the same website as the generated references.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 28. ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES\r\n\r\nStrictly avoid these patterns unless explicitly requested.\r\n\r\n### Layout slop\r\n- one giant unreadable collage\r\n- endless centered sections\r\n- identical card rows repeated section after section\r\n- cloned left-text/right-image blocks\r\n- fake complexity without hierarchy\r\n- decorative empty space with no purpose\r\n- cards-inside-cards-inside-cards\r\n- giant rounded wrapper sections around everything\r\n- overcompartmentalized dashboard framing\r\n\r\n### Visual slop\r\n- default purple/blue AI gradients\r\n- too many glowing edges\r\n- floating blobs everywhere\r\n- glassmorphism stacked without reason\r\n- random futuristic details with no structure\r\n- over-rendered noise that hides the layout\r\n\r\n### Typography slop\r\n- giant heading + weak tiny subcopy\r\n- too many font moods\r\n- awkward line breaks\r\n- lazy all-caps everywhere\r\n- generic gradient headline tricks\r\n\r\n### Content slop\r\nAvoid generic filler vibes like:\r\n- unleash\r\n- elevate\r\n- revolutionize\r\n- next-gen\r\n- seamless\r\n- transformative platform\r\n\r\nAvoid fake brand slop:\r\n- Acme\r\n- Nexus\r\n- Flowbit\r\n- Quantumly\r\n- NovaCore\r\n\r\nAvoid fake complexity slop:\r\n- pseudo-enterprise control labels\r\n- decorative system markers\r\n- filler status microcopy\r\n- fake operator / runtime / orchestration jargon unless truly central to the brand\r\n\r\n### Density slop\r\n- over-packed sections\r\n- card overload\r\n- tiny spacing between major sections\r\n- visually exhausting walls of content\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 30. SECTION RHYTHM RULE\r\n\r\nA high-end site does not feel like the same block repeated forever.\r\n\r\nVary section rhythm across the page by changing:\r\n- density\r\n- image-to-text ratio\r\n- alignment\r\n- scale\r\n- whitespace\r\n- card grouping\r\n- background intensity\r\n- visual tempo\r\n\r\nBut:\r\n- keep the page coherent\r\n- keep spacing controlled\r\n- avoid random jumps\r\n- keep each section clean enough to analyze well\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 32. Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.\n\nActions enable users to interact with your product or service right inside Gmail.\n\nFor example, when you send a notification that a magazine subscription is about to expire, you can present the option to renew it right from the notification.\n\nYou can declare actions in two ways: in-app actions or go-to actions. Gmail supports multiple types of actions.\n\n## In-app actions\n\nGmail handles in-app actions in place without sending the user to another website. These actions include one-click actions.\n\n### One-click action\n\nIn many scenarios, the user must confirm a predefined request. For example, when a user registers for a website, they receive an email asking them to confirm their registration. Similarly, a movie or music recommendation service can prompt a user to add items to a queue to enjoy later.\n\nImage: A Confirmation Button in Gmail\nOne-click actions in Gmail\n\nTo learn more, see the one-click action reference.\n\n## Go-to actions\n\nFor more complex interactions, use go-to actions to provide a direct link to the page where the user can perform the action. Clicking the button redirects the user to the page specified in the action definition.\n\nUse go-to actions for interactions that require multiple steps or significant data entry that users can\'t perform from the inbox. For example, an airline sending a check-in reminder can add a go-to action to direct the user to the airline website to select a seat or request an upgrade.\n\nImage: A Go-To Action in Gmail\nGo-to actions in Gmail\n\nTo learn more, see the go-to action reference.\n\n## Further reading\n\n  * Declare actions\nNote: Some schemas that Google uses are still going through the standardization process of Schema.org and might change in the future. <proposed_plan>
# Match the Calendly confirmation experience with LSAT U branding

## Summary

Use the supplied screenshot as the visual source of truth for both the confirmation email and the booking-success page. Preserve its restrained layout and information hierarchy, replacing every Calendly element with LSAT U branding and real booking data.

## Confirmation email

- Send from `LSAT U <noreply@lsatprep.study>`.
- Replace the current decorative gold confirmation card with the screenshot’s clean, white, centered email layout.
- Reproduce the visible structure:
  - Centered LSAT U logo
  - Light dotted divider
  - Left-aligned content column
  - `Hi [first name],`
  - `Your LSAT U session has been scheduled.`
  - Bold field labels with values beneath them
  - Event type
  - Invitee name
  - Invitee email
  - Date and time
  - Duration
  - Timezone
  - Location: Google Meet
- Use LSAT U’s existing typography and colors while matching the screenshot’s generous whitespace, narrow content width, light dividers, and minimal styling.
- Keep a Google Meet button lower in the email, followed by plain fallback links for clients that block styled buttons.
- Change the inaccurate sentence to: “Your Google Calendar invitation has been sent.”
- Remove “is on its way” and do not imply that the LSAT U confirmation email is waiting for calendar creation.
- Populate duration and timezone from the booking instead of hardcoding 70 minutes and Toronto.
- Build with email-safe tables and inline styles so Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, and mobile clients remain visually consistent.

## Gmail event panel

- Continue creating the real Google Calendar event with the invitee as an attendee, Google Meet attached, and `sendUpdates: "all"`.
- Add validated `EventReservation` structured metadata to the LSAT U confirmation email with the event title, attendee, start time, location, reservation number, and secure reservation URL.
- Add a Gmail `ViewAction` targeting the booking’s protected reservation page.
- Validate the markup with Google’s Email Markup Tester.
- Prepare the required Google sender-registration submission using the production sender, matching SPF or DKIM, `From`, and return-path domains. Google requires registration before marked-up production emails reliably receive enhanced Gmail treatment. [Google registration requirements](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/markup/registering-with-google)
- Treat Gmail’s blue event panel as an enhancement, not part of the HTML email. Gmail controls its exact appearance, labels, conflict warnings, and available buttons. LSAT U can provide the correct event metadata but cannot force Gmail to render an identical panel. [EventReservation specification](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/markup/reference/types/EventReservation)

## Confirmation page

- Show “You are scheduled!” immediately after payment confirmation.
- Mirror the earlier Calendly confirmation-page structure:
  - Sent-calendar-invitation message
  - Calendar-only primary action
  - Session-details panel
  - Attendee name
  - Localized date and time
  - Duration
  - Timezone
  - Google Meet availability note
  - Diagonal “Powered by LSAT U” corner ribbon
- While Google is still creating the event, show “Preparing your calendar invitation” and keep the calendar action disabled.
- Continue polling after the booking becomes `booked`.
- Replace the preparing state automatically with “A calendar invitation has been sent to your email address” and enable “Open Invitation” when the Google event URL becomes available.
- If Google is delayed, keep the booking confirmed and display a recovery message instead of spinning indefinitely.

## Backend and interface changes

- Persist the timezone selected during booking.
- Extend the capability-protected status response with `attendee_name`, `event_label`, `duration_minutes`, `timezone`, `calendar_ready`, and `calendar_url`.
- Resolve `calendar_url` from the mirrored Google event only after validating the booking token.
- Make the outbox worker claim newly unblocked confirmation-email jobs again after calendar promotion, so the email can send in the same webhook-triggered run.
- Preserve idempotency and the required ordering: payment finalized, calendar and Meet created, Google invitation sent, confirmation email sent.

## Verification

- Snapshot-test the email at desktop and mobile widths against the supplied reference.
- Render-test Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Mail output.
- Test real booking values, long names, different durations, multiple timezones, daylight-saving transitions, and missing optional notes.
- Test the immediate confirmation page, calendar-preparing transition, successful calendar link, delayed-calendar recovery, and invalid booking tokens.
- Verify the structured metadata with Google’s official validator.
- After deployment, perform one separately authorized $1 production booking and verify Stripe payment, calendar invitation, Meet link, Gmail presentation, confirmation page, and LSAT U email.
- Lovable deployment or any action that may consume Lovable credits requires Joshua’s fresh confirmation immediately before execution.

## Assumptions

- “Exactly” means faithfully reproducing the reference email’s layout and hierarchy with LSAT U branding and booking-specific content.
- Gmail’s surrounding interface and generated blue event panel cannot be pixel-controlled by the email template.
- Google may still require the recipient to accept an external invitation depending on that recipient’s Calendar settings.
</proposed_plan>

Buttons stay still; only the wordmark carries the sheen. */\r\n  background: linear-gradient(120deg, #4f0d1c, #6e1423 45%, #8e1d3a) !important;\r\n  color: #fff !important;\r\n}\r\n\r\n.holo-surface:hover { filter: brightness(1.12); }\r\n\r\n.holo-ring { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px hsl(347 70% 35% / 0.35), 0 8px 30px hsl(347 70% 25% / 0.12); }\r\n\r\n/* Soft burgundy-tinted elevation, the Calendly modal-shadow trick re-tinted. */\r\n.booking-shadow { box-shadow: 0 24px 72px hsl(345 60% 20% / 0.09), 0 0 20px hsl(345 60% 20% / 0.06); }\r\n\r\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\r\n  .holo-surface { animation: none; }\r\n  .single-session-page *,\r\n  .single-session-page *::before,\r\n  .single-session-page *::after {\r\n    scroll-behavior: auto !important;\r\n'}]

# LSAT U burgundy booking confirmation

## Summary

Match the supplied Calendly reference using LSAT U branding and its existing burgundy palette. The email body and confirmation page will use burgundy instead of blue. Gmail’s generated event panel may remain blue because Google controls that interface.

## Visual specification

- Use LSAT U’s production booking color:
  - Primary: `hsl(347 70% 27%)`, approximately `#75152A`
  - Dark gradient: `#4F0D1C → #6E1423 → #8E1D3A`
  - White button and ribbon text
- Use exact inline hex colors in email HTML because email clients cannot access the website’s CSS variables.
- Preserve the reference’s white background, generous spacing, narrow content column, understated dividers, and simple typography.
- Replace the blue Calendly logo with the LSAT U mark in burgundy.
- Use burgundy for buttons, links, important icons, and the “Powered by LSAT U” ribbon.
- Do not make the entire email burgundy or reproduce any Calendly branding.

## Confirmation email

- Recreate the reference structure:
  - Centered burgundy LSAT U logo
  - Light divider
  - `Hi [first name],`
  - `Your LSAT U session has been scheduled.`
  - Event type
  - Invitee name and email
  - Date, time, duration, and timezone
  - Google Meet location
- Change the outdated message to: “Your Google Calendar invitation has been sent.”
- Keep a burgundy Google Meet button and plain fallback link.
- Use booking-derived duration and timezone instead of hardcoded values.
- Build with email-safe tables and inline styles for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, and mobile clients.

## Gmail event panel

- Continue sending the actual Google Calendar invitation automatically with the attendee and Meet link.
- Add validated `EventReservation` metadata and a secure reservation action.
- Register the production sender with Google if LSAT U qualifies for enhanced Gmail markup.
- Accept that Gmail controls the generated panel’s blue background, button labels, conflict warnings, and final appearance. LSAT U cannot recolor Gmail’s own interface.

## Confirmation page

- Show “You are scheduled!” immediately after payment.
- Use the same burgundy palette for the success icon, calendar button, links, borders, and diagonal “Powered by LSAT U” ribbon.
- Display attendee, session type, date, time, duration, timezone, and conferencing information.
- Provide one calendar-only “Open Invitation” action.
- Continue polling while the calendar invitation is prepared, then enable the button automatically.
- Show a recoverable confirmed state if Google Calendar is delayed.

## Backend and verification

- Persist the selected timezone.
- Extend the protected booking-status response with the display details, calendar readiness, and calendar URL.
- Allow the outbox worker to send newly unblocked confirmation emails during the same run after calendar creation.
- Preserve payment, calendar, invitation, and email idempotency.
- Compare desktop and mobile email renders against the supplied screenshot.
- Test Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, different durations and timezones, delayed calendar creation, and invalid booking tokens.
- Perform one separately authorized $1 production booking after deployment.
- Obtain fresh confirmation before any Lovable action that could consume credits.

## Assumptions

- “Instead of blue” applies to all LSAT U-controlled email and confirmation-page elements.
- Gmail’s surrounding interface and generated event panel are excluded because their colors cannot be controlled by LSAT U.
</proposed_plan>
